reports.title: Reports
reports.sub: Name CRM reports in your own words and add reports that live outside the CRM, so people can open them from the chat.
reports.deleteMsg: This report entry will be removed. The CRM report itself is not touched.
reports.empty: No report entries yet. The CRM reports people can see are found by their own names already; add an entry to give one a different name or search words.
reports.loadError: The report list could not be loaded.
reports.notPersistent: Entries are only kept in memory and are lost when the service restarts. Ask your administrator to set up the database connection.
reports.switchedOff: Finding reports from the chat is switched off (Settings > Features).
reports.noCrmReports: No CRM reports could be listed. Open the report table in Data access and make sure the service account may read it; external addresses still work.
reports.tryHelp: Type what a person would ask. You see which reports the chat would offer, using your own CRM rights.
reports.tryNotReport: This does not look like a request for a report, so the chat would answer it as a normal question.
reports.tryNone: No report matches. The chat would answer it as a normal question.
reports.fNameHelp: What people call this report. This name is shown in the chat.
reports.fKeywordsHelp: One per line, in every language you use (for example: hesap özeti). People find the report with these words too.
reports.fUrlHelp: A web address that starts with http:// or https://. No user name or password in it.
reports.fRecordEntity: Open for the record on screen (optional)
reports.fRecordEntityHelp: A table name such as account. When someone is on a form of that table, the report opens for that record.
reports.fRecordParamHelp: The name the address uses for the record id (for example accountId). It is added to the address.
reports.reason_description: The description is too long (at most 300 characters).
reports.reason_keywords: Too many or too long search words (at most 20 words, 60 characters each).
reports.reason_target: Choose either a CRM report or an external address, not both.
reports.reason_url: Enter a valid http:// or https:// address without a user name or password.
reports.reason_record_entity: The table name may only contain lower-case letters, digits and underscores.
reports.reason_record_param: Enter the record parameter name (letters, digits, underscore) when an external report opens for a record.
reports.reason_limit: The catalog is full. Raise Reports:MaxEntries in Settings or delete entries.
perm.Reports.Manage: Manage the report catalog: give CRM reports a company name and search words, and add reports that live outside the CRM (for example a reporting-server address). Entries hold names and addresses, never report data; every change is audited
setting.Reports:MaxEntries: Most entries the report catalog may hold.
howto.reports.what: Lets people open reports from the chat. CRM reports they can see are found by name already; here you give them your own names and search words, or add reports that are not in the CRM.
howto.reports.s1: Click Add report and type the name people use.
howto.reports.s2: Choose a CRM report, or enter an external address.
howto.reports.s3: Add search words in every language you use.
howto.reports.s4: Optional: type a table name so the report opens for the record on screen.
howto.reports.s5: Use Try a question to check what the chat offers, then save.
howto.reports.r4v: Asked “hesap özeti raporunu aç” on an account form, the chat shows the report and opens it for that account
howto.reports.tip: The chat never sees report data. People only get CRM reports their own CRM rights allow; external addresses are offered to everyone, so add only addresses that are safe for all your users.
